gl-issue.description: GitLab issue: desc, comments, images, related MRs. A truncated description says so twice — in the header and at the cut — with the exact char count withheld. :full = no truncation, all comments

gl-mr.description: MR review: branch, pipeline, approval, linked issue, diff stat, per-file name-status (A/D/R/M) list, comments. A truncated description says so twice — in the header and at the cut — with the exact char count withheld. :status = slim merge-state only. :full uncaps the description, the file list + comments

gl-mrs.description: MR triage board: list MRs (default author=@me), sorted failing-first. Per MR: pipeline status (failed→job name), approval state, age, diff size, watch-state, conflict/draft/threads flags + actionable footer. Filters (comma-sep): author/reviewer/assignee/label/milestone/source-branch/target-branch/state/per. Flags: nopipe, iids, failed. A token outside those two lists, or a state outside opened/merged/closed/all, is REFUSED (exit 1, no board) rather than dropped. Enrichment calls run in parallel.

gl-issue-create.description: Create a GitLab issue from a JSON/TOML payload file. Supports milestone_id, labels, assignee_ids, estimate (quick action), and issue links.

gl-pipeline.description: Pipeline jobs by stage with statuses + failed job IDs. Default collapses manual/created/skipped bulk to a count. :active = running/pending only; :failed = failed jobs + IDs/URLs

gl-runners.description: Runner fleet health: one row per runner with type, status, heartbeat age, live job count and queue depth, sorted worst-health first. Joins the runner list with per-runner detail (tags, run_untagged, contacted_at) and the pending/running job queue to derive STARVED — pending jobs whose tags match only runners that stopped heartbeating, which GitLab still reports as online+idle. :full adds project scope, timeouts, versions; :queue groups pending/running jobs by the runners allowed to take them. Per-runner detail calls run in parallel.

gl-api.description: GET any GitLab REST path when no specialised gl-* op covers it (members, access tokens, deploy keys, protected branches, events, users). GET-only by design and the method is pinned, not defaulted: the op forwards no flags and refuses a flag-shaped path, naming glab for writes. A page that came back exactly per_page long is reported INCOMPLETE with the boundary it compared against - never as the whole list - and the comparison uses min(per_page,100) because GitLab silently caps per_page at 100. :full follows every page. The whole body is fenced as remote text; a non-JSON body is labelled NOT JSON and shown verbatim rather than parsed with a shrug. Emission budgeted by GL_API_MAX_BYTES (default 65536): an array is cut by item so the JSON stays valid and says 'N of M items shown', anything else is cut by characters and says it no longer parses

gl-job.description: Why job failed: MR ctx + error patterns + log tail. Argv is checked before anything is fetched (#1145): a non-numeric job id and a MODE outside fail/errors/raw/grep are both REFUSED with nothing read, and a ':' inside :grep:PATTERN is REJOINED rather than truncated, with a note saying how the pattern was read; '|' needs no escape. Shared with gh-job via presets/_job_argv.py. :fail (alias :errors) = matched failure blocks only, no tail — the tight triage view, per-job patterns; :raw dumps full trace; :raw:START[:END] slices lines (1-indexed, inclusive); :raw:-N is the last N lines, so the tail can be asked for without knowing the total; a START past the end returns the tail of the width requested and says so rather than declining; :grep:PATTERN ad-hoc regex over the trace (literal fallback, context, tail on no-match; emission budgeted by GL_JOB_GREP_MAX_BYTES, default 65536 — a capped view says so in its header AND footer with an exact 'N of M matching lines shown' and names bytes, not a match limit, as what cut). Cause markers (Caused by / Exception: / SQLSTATE / Exit Code / crash) are always matched on top of the patterns, and a failed job matching nothing is reported as unclassified with a log tail — never as 'no errors'
